negative_findings.description: K&H Bank (KBC group) — repeated Hungarian-language searches on kh.hu for beszállítói regisztráció, szállítóinknak, beszerzési alapelvek and beszállítói etikai kódex returned only retail/insurance customer portals and the career portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: No vendor registration page, no RFP page, no procurement contact found on kh.hu. Only the K&H Csoport fenntarthatósági irányelvek document describes supplier CSR contractual requirements.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: K&H is a top-3 Hungarian bank; its IT/facilities spend is entirely invisible externally. Access must be pursued via KBC group procurement or relationship channels, not open sources.

negative_findings.description: MBH Bank — no szállítói/beszállítói portál, no vendor registration and no RFP page located; searches surfaced only the MBH Beszállítói Faktoring (supply-chain finance) product and the merchant (kereskedői) POS portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only public sourcing evidence is the procurement/bidding chapter of the MBH Etikai Kódex.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: MBH is Hungary's second-largest bank and a large post-merger consolidation buyer; the absence of any public channel means its sourcing is trackable only via ethics-code language, MNB outsourcing regime, press and direct contact.

negative_findings.description: GRÁNIT Bank — Hungarian searches on beszerzés, beszállító, pályázat and ajánlatkérés returned no procurement or supplier page at all; the only procurement-adjacent hit was Gránit's participation, alongside MBH and OTP, as a bidder in the MFB Pont Plusz public procurement.
negative_findings.result_summary: Zero vendor-facing content located for Gránit Bank.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Gránit is the fastest-growing digital bank in the cell and a likely buyer of payments/IT services, but is entirely opaque from open sources; monitoring must rely on press, EKR bidder records and vendor-side announcements.

negative_findings.description: The Hungarian term 'beszállítói' is heavily overloaded: at MBH, UniCredit and others 'beszállítói finanszírozás / beszállítói faktoring / beszállítói program' means reverse-factoring supply-chain finance SOLD to clients, not the bank's own purchasing.
negative_findings.result_summary: The majority of bank-site hits for 'beszállítói' were supply-chain-finance products, not procurement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated Hungarian collection on 'beszállítói' will be dominated by false positives; queries must pair it with beszerzés / szállítói regisztráció / pályáztatás / ajánlatkérés and exclude faktoring / finanszírozás.

negative_findings.description: None of the nine private banks in this cell publishes open tender notices (versenyfelhívás / ajánlati felhívás) the way Magyar Telekom does. OTP explicitly routes RFx through invitation-only SAP Ariba events; Erste routes them through the Erste Group Procurements online platform.
negative_findings.result_summary: No open RFP/RFI listings found for any private Hungarian bank.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell rationale: for these banks, only onboarding/policy pages and platform identification are collectable; award-level intelligence must come from indirect sources (vendor press releases, registry, MNB outsourcing, MFB benchmarks).

negative_findings.description: The MNB outsourcing (kiszervezés) register — the richest structured bank-to-vendor contract dataset in Hungary — is a supervisory filing, not a public register.
negative_findings.result_summary: The 58/2015 MNB rendelet and 7/2020 ajánlás describe mandatory notification and register content, but the data itself sits with the supervisor via the ERA portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets a hard ceiling on open-source vendor-contract visibility; only the rules, not the records, are collectable. Any future DORA register-of-information disclosure would be a step change and should be watched.

negative_findings.description: erstegroupprocurement.com and epp.unicreditbank.hu/partnerkapu were identified by reference/search but not fetched in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs recorded with reduced confidence; scope and liveness unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Both are plausible direct vendor entry points; a single failed or skipped fetch is not evidence they are dead or irrelevant and they should be checked in the deterministic verification pass.

brief: Hungary's systemic private banks buy entirely outside the public procurement system, and only three of the nine maintain a genuinely vendor-facing public presence: OTP (a full szállítóknak hub with self-registration to vendorman@otpbank.hu, prequalification, a partner code of ethics and a gradual SAP Ariba rollout), Erste Bank Hungary (an unusually informative CSR page naming the Erste Group Hungarian procurement unit as exclusive procurement provider, with supplier counts and an EUR 100k CSR threshold, sourcing run on the Erste Group Procurements platform), and Raiffeisen (a published procurement GTC PDF). CIB and K&H disclose procurement principles only inside CSR/sustainability documents, MBH only inside its code of ethics, while UniCredit, Gránit and the Magyar Bankholding legacy names yield nothing vendor-facing at all — and no bank in the cell publishes open RFx, so real tender traffic lives on invitation-only e-sourcing platforms. The practical collection strategy is therefore: monitor the handful of onboarding/policy pages and their PDFs for change; identify the platform each bank sources on; and fill the award-level blind spot indirectly through MFB's published EKR summaries as a category benchmark, EKR/Közbeszerzési Értesítő bidder records, MNB's outsourcing regime, registry data and vendor-side announcements. Note a major vocabulary trap: 'beszállítói' on Hungarian bank sites usually means supply-chain-finance products sold to clients, not the bank's own purchasing.
